type: Locally frozen deterministic mathematical check; not external preregistration or an empirical experiment
knowledge_before_freeze: The analytic finite-horizon cancellation for shared deterministic calendar-time rates and its two-transient-state representation were derived before this numerical check. No empirical outcomes are used.
question: Does the family-selected prospective random-tag survivor function remain independent of selection horizon under shared nonconstant calendar-time birth and death rates?
assumptions: All living cells share deterministic calendar-time rates lambda(t), mu(t)
Each tagged division chooses one daughter uniformly and independently of future fate
Retain founders iff any family descendant is alive at T
Compare only t <= T with positive inclusion probability
not_covered: The actual tag lifetime beyond T
method_1: Solve backward family survival ODE h_s=(mu-lambda)*h+lambda*h*h, h(T)=1; independently integrate the discarded-sister Poisson functional A=exp(-integral_0^t lambda(u)*h(u,T)du); Q_PGFL=exp(-M(t))*(1-(1-h(t,T))*A)/h(0,T).
method_2: Direct quadrature of Q=exp(-L(t))+exp(-M(t))*integral_0^t lambda(u)*exp(M(u)-L(u))du, using analytic cumulative rates L and M.
method_3: Forward ODE x1'=-lambda*x1, x2'=lambda*x1-mu*x2, x1(0)=1,x2(0)=0; Q=x1+x2.

numerics.piecewise_policy: Split ODEs and quadratures at known discontinuities; use correct one-sided segment rates for ODE endpoints.

checks: All three survivor functions agree at every fixed case/time
PGFL estimates agree across different horizons at shared absolute times
Probabilities stay in [0,1] and are nonincreasing with t
All zero-birth/zero-death control Q values equal one
Constant cases recover the earlier hypoexponential or Erlang-two formula
failure_policy: Retain every case and failure. Do not change grids or thresholds after first numerical run; any correction is separately labeled.
empirical_data: None; no fitting, source-outcome calibration, or biological inference.
